item.title: Mamdani’s influence sharply felt as Democrats win big in affordability election
item.description:
New York mayor’s cost-of-living message inspired not just progressives but centrists in red states – and voters agreed

Zohran Mamdani wasn’t running in the midterm elections. In races across the country, however, the New York City’s mayor influence could be seen, as Democrats adopted a laser focus on affordability and downed establishment opponents.

From Texas to Kansas, Democrats ran by pointing out the high cost of living and, frequently, by linking that to billionaires.

item.title: International student enrollments at US universities plunge this fall, data shows
item.description:
Report finds fewer international students studying in US amid Trump’s crackdowns on immigration and education

Fewer international students are studying at US universities as the Trump administration cracks down on immigration and reshapes higher education, data released on Monday show.

Overall, US campuses saw a 9% decrease in international enrollment this fall compared with last year, according to a survey from the Institute of International Education. And the number of new students entering the United States for the first time fell by 15%.

Researchers forced to scrap original studies as NIH rethinks grants not in ‘alignment’ with administration’s priorities

Dr Jade Pagkas-Bather received her first grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) in June 2025 – a milestone in any researcher’s career.

She planned to study basic income as a medical intervention: her randomized control trial would test whether monthly grants of $500-cash helped poor, HIV-positive young people in Chicago stick with treatment. Her hypothesis was as straightforward as it was cutting.
